title: Not every
problem is
in the code.
boundary.lead: I can tell when continuing with a given approach makes sense and when it brings more complexity than value.

decision.currentText: A problem or limitation appears during development.
decision.question: Can it be fixed without changing the approach?

stay.title: The problem is local
stay.text: The problem comes from a specific part of the implementation.
stay.meta: The fix is limited to the implementation; the underlying approach stays the same.

rise.title: It keeps coming back
rise.text: Each change moves the problem somewhere else or requires another exception.
rise.meta: This signals that the approach itself needs to change.

layers.title: Data model
layers.text: How different cases and rules are handled.

layers.title: Data / state
layers.text: Where the source of truth lives.

principles.title: The number of exceptions keeps growing
principles.text: Each new case requires a special path or workaround.

principles.title: A small change stops being local
principles.text: A simple change triggers a cascade of changes across the application.

principles.title: A change in one place breaks something elsewhere
principles.text: Fixing one case creates a problem or regression elsewhere.

principles.title: Multiple sources of truth emerge
principles.text: The same information is maintained independently in several places and requires synchronization.

boundary.musicNote: I encountered this way of thinking earlier in audio production, where the initial concept often evolves with each new version.
